trailmix: htmx outerHTML vs innerHTML when swapping a table row?

Use `hx-swap="outerHTML"` with `hx-target="closest tr"` and have the Django view return a full `<tr>`. innerHTML would put your new `<tr>` inside the old one, and browsers drop or mangle a nested tr. With outerHTML the whole row is replaced, attributes included.

events.text: b-tree vs gin index, short version

B-tree: one sorted entry per row value. Good for equality, ranges and ORDER BY on scalar columns. GIN: an inverted index, one entry per element inside a value (array items, jsonb keys, text lexemes) pointing to the rows that contain it. Good for "contains" queries, slower to update.

what does terraform plan -refresh-only do vs a normal plan

A normal plan compares your config to the real infrastructure and proposes changes to make reality match the config. `-refresh-only` ignores your config changes: it only reads the real resources and shows how the state file would be updated to match them (drift someone made by hand, for example). Applying it rewrites state, never infrastructure.

events.text: what does npm link actually do under the hood

Two symlinks. Run in a package folder, it links that folder into npm's global node_modules and links each `bin` entry into the global bin dir, so the command is on your PATH and points at your working copy. Run as `npm link <name>` in another project, it symlinks that global entry into the project's node_modules. Nothing is copied, so edits (or rebuilds) show up immediately.

whats a monorepo exactly? my nephew asked and i totally fumbled it

One git repository that holds several projects that could have lived in separate repos: say a website, a server and a shared library. They share one history and one set of tools, so a change that touches all three is a single commit and they can't drift out of sync. The trade-off is that the repo gets big, and you need tooling to build and test only the parts that changed.

events.text: trailmix q: postgres or sqlite for a one user app?

SQLite. One user means no write concurrency to speak of, Django supports it well, and backups are copying one file. Turn on WAL mode and you're set. Move to Postgres only if you add more users, need full-text search beyond basics, or host somewhere with an ephemeral disk.
